lede: Asia tech crash (Kospi -7%+, Nikkei -4%+) on AI debt worries after hot CPI; Nasdaq futures -1.3%; yields and oil lower, gold up.

single_name_moves.venue: Wed close; EPS $0.91 vs $1.09 est after $1.2B fine (Reuters, Investopedia)

geo_headlines: ASIA TECH CRASHED OVERNIGHT. South Korea's Kospi fell more than 7% and Japan's Nikkei more than 4% (CNBC); the Kosdaq dropped 8%, triggering a 20-minute halt (investingLive). Samsung fell 9.5% and SK Hynix 6.1% (DPA). **The driver is worry about AI infrastructure debt as rates rise: CoreWeave fell nearly 17% Wednesday and its 2032 bond yielded 15% (Investopedia), and Broadcom's CEO again warned about AI financing in Singapore (DPA).**

HOT CPI HIT TECH WEDNESDAY. September CPI rose 3.7% from a year ago vs 3.6% expected, and core 2.6% vs 2.5%; core rose 0.3% on the month vs 0.2%. Gasoline rose 9.1% and was about half the headline increase (CNBC). The S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94, 1.28% below its October 6 record close; the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.02% and chips 4.3%, a sixth straight loss (Reuters). Oracle fell 8.8% and Dell 11.4%.

FUTURES: NASDAQ DOWN AGAIN. Nasdaq 100 futures 29,794 (-1.29%), S&P 500 futures 7,743.50 (-0.34%) as of 6:50 AM ET. TSMC posted record profit of NT$763 billion, up 69%, with a 66.4% gross margin (TrendForce), but that has not lifted chips. Anthropic reportedly told investors third-quarter revenue rose 45% to about $16.8 billion, slower growth than before (Investing.com).

RATES: HIKE ODDS UP, YIELDS DOWN. FedWatch, as of Wednesday 10/14: October hike 29.9%, December 89.5%. San Francisco Fed President Daly said further hikes are "more likely than not" but signaled no need to move in October (investingLive). The 10-year fell to 5.144% overnight (Reuters); gold rose to $4,175.10 (+1.6%).

OIL: ARAMCO HQ HIT; BRENT EASES. A Houthi missile hit an Aramco building in Dhahran overnight after a Saudi-led strike on a Yemen fuel depot (BBC). Brent December $104.54 (-1.4%), WTI November $95.06 (flat), after Wednesday settles of $106.06 and $95.09 (Rigzone). The Beige Book said higher oil prices were reported across all 12 districts (Federal Reserve).

TODAY: PPI, RETAIL SALES, CLAIMS. 8:30 AM: PPI (BLS) and September retail sales (Census), consensus +0.3%; jobless claims, 199,000 expected. Friday: options expiration. Australia lost 39,300 jobs in September vs gains expected; unemployment 4.7% (ABS); AUD/JPY -0.9%.
client_frame_short: This is the week the AI trade met higher rates. Wednesday's inflation report came in hot, mostly because of gasoline, and the market now worries that rising borrowing costs will squeeze the companies building AI data centers on debt. **Korea fell more than 7% and Japan more than 4% overnight, and Nasdaq futures are down another 1.3%, but the Dow is nearly flat and bonds rallied: this is a tech correction, not a broad market break.** For clients: diversification is doing its job, and long-term plans do not change.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is a sharp pullback in AI stocks, set off by Wednesday's inflation report.

What happened: consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past year, a bit hotter than expected, and gasoline was about half the increase. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, was 2.6%. That raised the odds of another Fed hike, and the market sold the stocks most sensitive to borrowing costs: the AI infrastructure names. CoreWeave, which borrows heavily to build data centers, fell nearly 17%, and its bonds yield about 15%. Oracle fell 8.8% and Dell 11.4%.

Overnight it spread: Korea fell more than 7%, Japan more than 4%, and Nasdaq futures are down another 1.3%.

The context: the S&P 500 is 1.28% below its October 6 record. The Nasdaq 100 is about 4% below its record, and chip stocks are about 20% below their June peak. The Dow was nearly flat Wednesday, Apple closed above $5 trillion, and TSMC just reported record profits. The demand for AI is real; the question the market is asking is who pays for it and at what interest rate.

The bond market is helping: the 10-year yield fell to about 5.14% overnight and gold rose, which is what diversification is supposed to do on a day like this.

Why it matters: portfolios concentrated in AI and chips are feeling this; balanced portfolios much less. Corrections of this kind are normal inside long bull markets, and selling into them has historically been costly. Rebalancing toward targets is the right move; abandoning the plan is not.

For clients, the message holds: high-quality bonds pay more than 5% for a decade, and long-term equity plans do not need changing. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Wednesday 5.19%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Wednesday 5.52%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (now $104.54).
